title: Great Fire picture sequence sheet
subject: History
unit: Summer 1: The Great Fire of London, 1666 (Bright Lights, Big City)
source: Seeded from history/y1 lesson 6 (Great Fire picture sequence sheet (portal printable; buildings and objects only))
intro: Lesson 6: The Great Fire of London, 1666. To understand why the Great Fire of London spread and how we know about it

questions.q: When did the Great Fire start?
questions.model: I look at the title. It says the Great Fire of London, 1666. So it started in 1666.

questions.q: Name one thing that helped the fire spread.
questions.a: Wind, dry weather or wooden houses

questions.q: Put four pictures in order: the bakery, the fire spreading, the buckets, the new brick houses. Draw buildings and flames only.
questions.a: 1 bakery, 2 fire spreading, 3 buckets and fire hooks, 4 new brick houses
questions.model: Teacher shows which comes first: the bakery, where it all began.

questions.a: For example: The wind blew the fire from house to house.

questions.q: Why is a diary good evidence?
Big question: how did one small fire burn most of a city?
questions.a: Wind and dry weather blew it from wooden house to wooden house
